headline: Brisk-S costs least but trails on quality and on confirming account changes; Atlas-M closes most of the gap at a mid price; Atlas-L leads at the top price. No price per point of quality was set.
lede: A point of overall quality costs {price.brisk-s.atlas-m.overall.per_point_low_unpaired} to {price.brisk-s.atlas-m.overall.per_point_high_unpaired} per thousand conversations from Brisk-S to Atlas-M, and {price.atlas-m.atlas-l.overall.per_point_low_unpaired} to {price.atlas-m.atlas-l.overall.per_point_high_unpaired} from Atlas-M to Atlas-L. A declared price per point would decide it.

caveats.material_if: High applies to the priced bands, which rest on overall quality from a judge calibrated on {judged.overall.calibration_ratings} human ratings with {judged.overall.agreement} agreement. The lean's reasons rest on the behaviour checks, whose judge is not described: confirming account changes, declining to speculate, and Atlas-L not being told apart from Atlas-M on any check. Those reasons would move if that judge is lenient or harsh toward one model, and stay unconfirmed until the calibration step is done.

Only for a reader who wants a call rather than a priced trade: with no price per point and no floor set, the choice among the {count.frontier.overall|words} models on the price frontier stays the owner's.

Only for the gaps not told apart, such as Atlas-L against Atlas-M on the behaviour checks, or Open-70B against Brisk-S on overall quality: every gap here is read unpaired, which errs wide, so a paired read could separate them; the gaps already clear of zero would only narrow their intervals.

Only if a fresh run reads Atlas-L's edge over Atlas-M lower, as the top of several candidates tends to: that would make the step up to Atlas-L dearer per point, which favours the lean rather than reversing it.

caveats.label: Cost routing unknown
caveats.material_if: Only if another provider serves these models at different prices: the snapshot names no provider for any model, so every cost and price per point holds for this run's routing alone.

decision.text: Moving up from Brisk-S ({cost_per_1k.brisk-s} per thousand conversations) to Atlas-M ({cost_per_1k.atlas-m}) or Atlas-L ({cost_per_1k.atlas-l}) buys overall quality in every task that carries traffic and better behaviour on the checks that guard users; each step up also adds latency.

If a point of overall quality is worth less than {price.brisk-s.atlas-m.overall.per_point_low_unpaired} to {price.brisk-s.atlas-m.overall.per_point_high_unpaired} per thousand conversations, Brisk-S is the buy; between that band and {price.atlas-m.atlas-l.overall.per_point_low_unpaired} to {price.atlas-m.atlas-l.overall.per_point_high_unpaired}, Atlas-M; above it, Atlas-L. Inside either band this run does not settle the pick.

Ours, not a declared rule: Atlas-M, for any price per point in the middle band. It avoids Brisk-S's misses on confirming account changes and declining to speculate, while Atlas-L costs {cost.gap.atlas-l.atlas-m.multiple} what Atlas-M does and is not told apart from it on any behaviour check. Those reasons rest on an undescribed judge until it is calibrated.

Open-70B ({cost_per_1k.open-70b}) confirms before account changes less often than any other model ({task.trouble.open-70b.confirms.mean}). On price it sits off the frontier on point estimates only: its pooled overall quality ({pooled.overall.open-70b.mean}) is {price.brisk-s.open-70b.overall.gain} above Brisk-S's, an interval of {price.brisk-s.open-70b.overall.gain_interval_unpaired} not told apart from zero, so a point bought moving to it costs {price.brisk-s.open-70b.overall.per_point} at the estimate and as little as {price.brisk-s.open-70b.overall.per_point_low_unpaired} at the interval's top, inside the lower band.

Atlas-M's weak side is troubleshooting, where it trails Atlas-L by {compare.atlas-l.atlas-m.overall.task.trouble.difference|abs} points of overall quality. Speculation bait carries {task.specul.share} of traffic, so declining to speculate is read on a test set, not on live conversations.
The concierge owner declares a price per point of overall quality, or a floor on confirming before account changes; either turns this trade into a decision.

claims.text: Each step up the price frontier buys overall quality, and the step from Atlas-M to Atlas-L costs more per point than the step from Brisk-S to Atlas-M. Pooled by traffic, overall quality reads {pooled.overall.brisk-s.mean} for Brisk-S, {pooled.overall.atlas-m.mean} for Atlas-M and {pooled.overall.atlas-l.mean} for Atlas-L: the first step gains {price.brisk-s.atlas-m.overall.gain} points ({price.brisk-s.atlas-m.overall.gain_interval_unpaired}), the second {price.atlas-m.atlas-l.overall.gain} ({price.atlas-m.atlas-l.overall.gain_interval_unpaired}).

evidence.caption: Price per point of overall quality at each step, per thousand conversations; intervals are unpaired.

claims.text: Atlas-M scores above Brisk-S on overall quality in every task, by the most in troubleshooting ({compare.atlas-m.brisk-s.overall.task.trouble.difference|abs} points).

evidence.caption: Atlas-M minus Brisk-S on overall quality per task, with unpaired intervals.

claims.text: Brisk-S falls behind Atlas-M on the two behaviour checks that guard users most directly: Atlas-M confirms before account changes {compare.atlas-m.brisk-s.confirms.task.trouble.difference|abs} points more often, and declines speculation bait more often too.

evidence.caption: Atlas-M minus Brisk-S on confirming before account changes, read in troubleshooting, with its unpaired interval.
Atlas-M minus Brisk-S on declining to speculate, read on speculation bait, a test set with no live traffic, with its unpaired interval.

claims.text: Atlas-L scores above Atlas-M on overall quality in every task that carries traffic, by the most in troubleshooting; on speculation bait the two are not told apart.

evidence.caption: Atlas-L minus Atlas-M on overall quality per task, with unpaired intervals.

claims.text: Latency follows cost: Brisk-S answers fastest and Atlas-L slowest in every task that carries traffic, and no latency budget was declared.

evidence.caption: Latency from p50 to p95, per task that carries traffic.

explore.control: Price of one point of overall quality, per thousand conversations
explore.binds: Which model on the price frontier is the buy
explore.outcome: Brisk-S below {price.brisk-s.atlas-m.overall.per_point_low_unpaired} to {price.brisk-s.atlas-m.overall.per_point_high_unpaired}; Atlas-M from there to {price.atlas-m.atlas-l.overall.per_point_low_unpaired} to {price.atlas-m.atlas-l.overall.per_point_high_unpaired}; Atlas-L above. Open-70B is off the frontier on point estimates, but its gain over Brisk-S is not told apart from zero, so it could take part of the lower band.

explore.control: A floor on confirming before account changes, read on the point estimate
explore.binds: Whether Brisk-S and Open-70B remain options
explore.outcome: A floor above Brisk-S's {task.trouble.brisk-s.confirms.mean} and below Atlas-M's {task.trouble.atlas-m.confirms.mean} leaves Atlas-M the least costly option that meets it.

method.text: {scoreboard.atlas-m.cases} cases per model, split over the tasks the tables list; no model lost or failed a case. Repeats are not stated.
A judged score on every task, from a judge calibrated on {judged.overall.calibration_ratings} human ratings with {judged.overall.agreement} agreement.
Pass or fail judgements, each read in the one task that tests it; the snapshot does not say who judged them.

Overall quality across tasks is weighted by each task's traffic share; speculation bait carries {task.specul.share}, so it tests behaviour without moving the pooled score. The full-results tables list per-task scores only, so each model's pooled score is stated in the lead claim, and Open-70B's under why not.
At the level each table prints, uncorrected. With no control and no paired contrasts, every gap between two models combines their own intervals as independent, which errs wide.
Cost per thousand conversations as this run served each model; no provider is named and no monthly volume was declared.
p50 and p95 per task; no budget was declared.
No routed mix of models was run, and nothing was declared before the run: no gate, floor, margin or exchange rate.
